title: Build composition golden suite and opt-in real render tests
description:
## Objective
Cover fairy-tale and repository timelines across supported mechanics.

## Scope
- Illustrated story with narration and captions
- Technical episode with code/diagram overlays
- Mixed image dimensions and audio rates
- Cancellation and corrupt input scenarios
- Performance baseline for 3-8 minute output

## Boundaries and risks
- Preserve canonical workspace and contract ownership boundaries.
- Add deterministic tests for failure paths, cancellation, and restart where applicable.
- Do not hide a material downgrade or destructive migration behind a fallback.
design: Phase: release. Implement behind typed ports and versioned contracts. Keep diagnostics machine-readable and user-actionable. Update module documentation and fixtures together with behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] One command renders short golden clips locally
- [ ] CI can run reduced fixtures without paid services
- [ ] Reports validate against contracts and include no absolute secret paths
- [ ] Unit/integration tests cover success and relevant failure paths.
- [ ] Public contract and operator/contributor documentation are updated.

close_reason: Implemented timeline semantic validator (src/validator.ts) with typed contracts, injectable asset probe, stale-dependency checks, and comprehensive error diagnostics. 84 tests cover all acceptance criteria: invalid fixtures fail before FFmpeg, valid fixtures normalize deterministically, duration mismatches are rejected (never silently clamped), and documentation (API.md, CONTRIBUTING.md) is updated.

title: Deliver typed FFmpeg composition and delivery QA
description:
## Objective
Compile validated edit timelines into reproducible YouTube-ready videos and prove output quality with machine-readable reports.

## Delivery boundary
Complete all child beads to produce the module's MVP release. Cross-module integration uses released contracts and fakes before depending on live paid or hardware services.

## Planning rule
Child dependencies encode implementation order. A child is complete only when its acceptance criteria and tests are satisfied, not when code merely exists.
design: No arbitrary shell fragments. The compiler owns mechanics, never editorial choices.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed; module README and generated/operator documentation match behavior; clean checkout passes build, test, lint, contract, and release checks; no known P0/P1 defect remains.
